key_agent_trends: Coding-agent default autonomy is now a security surface: Auto Mode classifiers that score 0% ASR on lab suites still miss novel web-to-shell injection chains.
Usage rationing is colliding with always-on agent habits. Anthropic is converting a 50% Claude Code promo into a smaller permanent lift, a 17% cut versus current weekly caps.
Cloud platforms are productizing singleton, always-on personal agents instead of only request-scaled chat APIs.
Agentic coding is already changing software budgets: McKinsey finds 32% of orgs skipped at least one purchase because they could build it with coding agents.
Industrial firms are treating agents as workforce and workflow tools, not just chat, and budgeting retraining at fleet scale.

stories.headline: Claude Code Opus 5 Auto Mode hijacked by a website-summary prompt
stories.what_happened: Security researcher Johann Rehberger showed that Claude Code running Opus 5 in default Auto Mode can be steered into executing attacker-controlled code after a request to summarize a malicious website. The site fails WebFetch with HTTP 415, Claude falls back to curl, follows a redirect to a ZIP that includes a poisoned struct.py, and then writes its own Python decoder that imports the shadowed standard-library module. Small-sample tests reported 60-80% success across variants, including C2 callbacks and writes outside the workspace. The chain sits outside the held-out suite Anthropic used to report a 0.00% Auto Mode attack success rate.
stories.why_it_matters: Default-on agent autonomy plus web tools turns ordinary summarization into an RCE path. Classifier evals that score zero on disclosed suites do not cover novel multi-step tool fallbacks.

stories.headline: Anthropic will cut current Claude Code weekly limits 17% on September 14
stories.what_happened: On August 29 Anthropic's ClaudeDevs account said standard Claude Code weekly limits will rise 25% permanently on September 14 for Pro, Max, Team, and seat-based Enterprise plans. The current 50% promotional lift stays until then. Versus today's promo cap that is about a 17% reduction, which Anthropic stated explicitly. Help Center copy still documents the older promo ending August 31, so Sep 1-13 capacity depends on which notice users follow.
stories.why_it_matters: Teams that staffed long-running coding agents against the summer promo now have a hard capacity cut. It also shows how tightly frontier coding-agent supply is rationed.

stories.headline: Google Cloud Run instances preview targets always-on personal agents
stories.what_happened: Google Cloud introduced Cloud Run instances, a preview singleton runtime for long-lived stateful workloads such as personal agents. Unlike request-scaled Cloud Run services, each instance is one container with a stable HTTPS URL, optional stop/resume, and automatic restarts, with up to seven days of continuous runtime. Google priced a 1 vCPU / 1 GiB instance running 30 days at $5.70 and published a one-command OpenClaw deploy path using Cloud Storage for agent state.
stories.why_it_matters: Always-on agents need a cheap dedicated process, not a scale-to-zero API. This is infrastructure for personal and team agents that keep memory and inbound channels alive overnight.

stories.headline: McKinsey: 32% of orgs skipped a software purchase because coding agents could build it
stories.what_happened: McKinsey's State of AI in 2026 survey, published August 25 and widely reported over the weekend, found that 32% of respondents' organizations decided against buying at least one software product or feature because agentic coding tools could build it internally. Large enterprises scaling agents in one or more functions rose from 27% to 40%; smaller firms stayed flat at 22%. About two in ten respondents overall, and 31% at larger enterprises, said they are already scaling software coding agents. The skip-a-purchase rate was highest in technology (41%) and healthcare (39%).
stories.why_it_matters: Coding agents are no longer just a developer productivity add-on. They are starting to substitute for packaged software spend, which hits SaaS vendors and internal platform teams at the same time.

stories.headline: Caterpillar will spend $100M training 118,000 workers and is using agents on legacy code
stories.what_happened: Speaking with TechCrunch at Ai4, Caterpillar CTO Jaime Mineart said the company will spend $100 million over five years training its 118,000 employees in AI, autonomy, and robotics. Caterpillar already runs about 1.6 million connected assets and more than 16 petabytes of structured data into tools such as the voice-driven Cat AI Assistant for field techs. Mineart said the firm also uses AI agents to modernize legacy code, generate and test software, and catch defects earlier, applying the same change-management playbook it used for autonomous mining.
stories.why_it_matters: A large industrial OEM treating coding agents and technician assistants as part of a $100M workforce plan is a concrete enterprise deployment, not a lab demo.
